options.text: Quantum numbers $(n, l, m, s)$ are arbitrarily
All the quantum numbers $(n, 1, m, s)$ for any pair of electron in an atom can be identical under special circumstance
All the quantum numbers $(n, 1, m, s)$ may not be required to describe an electron of an atom completely
All the quantum numbers $(n, 1, m, s)$ are required to describe an electron of an atom completely

solution.text: All the quantum numbers $(n, l, m, s)$ are required to describe an electron of an atom completely. e.g., $n$ describes the position and energy of the electron in an orbit or shell. l is used to describe subshell and the shape of the orbital occupied by the electron. $m$ describes the preferred orientation of orbitals in space. s describes the spining of an electron on its axis.
